checks: every min <= max (A, BA, BB, C, E, F) and BB <= BA, GB <= GA for all 14 rows
D (nominal eye OD) equals the mean of (C+2E) at the lower and upper limits (|diff| <= 0.01 in) -> confirms that the two values printed per cell are lower/upper limits
F_min = BA_min + C_min + 2*E_min and F_max = BA_max + C_max + 2*E_max within 0.01 in -> the plain-pattern overall length F belongs to Style A (long shank)
all dimension columns grow monotonically with nominal size (D 1.19..8.50, tpi falls 20..4)
shape_hint: A forged steel eye bolt: a closed circular ring (eye) of round section E with inside diameter C and nominal outside diameter D forms the head; a straight cylindrical shank of diameter A runs down from the eye to a UNC threaded end (full thread length G, shank length B, overall length F measured from the top of the eye). The shoulder pattern adds a flat round collar (shoulder diameter J, height K, fillet radius R under it) between the eye and the shank.

role_map.BA_min: shank length, Style A (long), lower limit
role_map.BA_max: shank length, Style A (long), upper limit
role_map.BB_min: shank length, Style B (short), lower limit
role_map.BB_max: shank length, Style B (short), upper limit
role_map.E_min: eye section (ring wire) diameter lower limit
role_map.F_min: overall length lower limit (plain pattern, Style A)
role_map.F_max: overall length upper limit (plain pattern, Style A)

notes: ASME B18.15 forged eyebolts, inch. TABLE = Type 1 PLAIN pattern (straight shank) only, Styles A (long) and B (short). The sources print two values in each toleranced cell (e.g. eye ID '0.69 0.81'); they are not labelled in the web tables, but arithmetic shows they are lower/upper limits (D = mean of C+2E at both limits; F = B + C + 2E), so they are published here as _min/_max by inference - confirm labels against the standard's table before printing as 'min/max'. F (overall length) is for Style A (long shank); Style B overall length is not tabulated in these sources. Nominal sizes 1-1/8 and 2 dropped (see dropped); 2-1/2 has no shoulder pattern. SHOULDER PATTERN (Type 2) extras verified by >=3 sources, as lower/upper pairs (min/max), inches: shoulder-pattern overall length F_sh, eye-to-shoulder H, shoulder diameter J, shoulder height K, radius under shoulder R; the B, C, D, E, G dimensions are the same as the plain table. 1/4: F_sh=2.22/2.53, H=0.69/0.81, J=0.5/0.56, K=0.12/0.19, R=0.015/0.025 ; 5/16: F_sh=2.66/2.97, H=0.88/1.0, J=0.56/0.62, K=0.12/0.19, R=0.015/0.025 ; 3/8: F_sh=3.09/3.47, H=1.06/1.19, J=0.62/0.69, K=0.12/0.19, R=0.015/0.025 ; 7/16: F_sh=3.41/3.78, H=1.19/1.31, J=0.75/0.81, K=0.19/0.25, R=0.015/0.025 ; 1/2: F_sh=3.81/4.19, H=1.31/1.44, J=0.88/0.94, K=0.19/0.25, R=0.015/0.025 ; 9/16: F_sh=4.19/4.56, H=1.5/1.62, J=0.94/1.0, K=0.22/0.28, R=0.02/0.045 ; 5/8: F_sh=4.56/4.94, H=1.59/1.72, J=1.0/1.06, K=0.25/0.31, R=0.02/0.045 ; 3/4: F_sh=5.06/5.5, H=1.72/1.91, J=1.12/1.25, K=0.25/0.31, R=0.02/0.045 ; 7/8: F_sh=5.75/6.19, H=2.03/2.22, J=1.31/1.44, K=0.31/0.38, R=0.04/0.065 ; 1: F_sh=6.44/6.88, H=2.22/2.41, J=1.5/1.62, K=0.38/0.44, R=0.06/0.095 ; 1-1/4: F_sh=8.0/8.44, H=2.84/3.03, J=1.88/2.0, K=0.5/0.56, R=0.06/0.095 ; 1-1/2: F_sh=9.22/9.72, H=3.19/3.44, J=2.12/2.25, K=0.5/0.62, R=0.06/0.095 ; 1-3/4: F_sh=10.5/11.12, H=3.88/4.12, J=2.5/2.62, K=0.5/0.62, R=0.06/0.095 ; 2-1/2: (no shoulder-pattern row in the sources). 9/16 row: nan-long (and boltingspecialist for shoulder) print the size as '9/15' (typo) with identical values; these were not counted for the 9/16 plain row (support 3 = amesweb, torqbolt, fastenerz). Outliers found: amesweb plain F column is contaminated with shoulder-pattern F values (1, 1-1/8 ... 2 rows); nan-long plain table repeats B-style-B values in the C column for 1-1/4..2-1/2 sizes and prints 2.23/2.26 at 1-1/8; boltingspecialist 1-1/2 J=2.52 typo. Material/capacity standards: ASTM A489 (carbon steel), ASTM F541 (alloy steel) govern strength; not dimension sources.

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched live: amesweb.info, torqbolt.com, fastenerz.com, nan-long.com, boltingspecialist type-2 (all 200); parsed plain-pattern tables (16 sizes x A,BA,BB,C,D,E,F,GA,GB, both limits) and shoulder tables (15 sizes). Matrix of the 14 record rows x 17 cols x 4 sources: every record cell found in >=3 sources; deviations only in dropped cols (AMES F col contaminated by shoulder-F at 1,1-1/8..2; AMES E at 1-1/4,1-3/4; nan-long BB at 1-1/4..2-1/2). Kept columns d_nom, tpi, D, GA, GB: 4/4 pages agree for ALL 16 sizes (also 1-1/8 and 2). tpi checked vs UNC series.
problems: ALL 12 *_min/*_max columns: no source header says min/max. Sources print two unlabeled numbers per cell (ames: two table lines per size; torq: staggered second line; fastenerz/nan-long/boltport: 'a b' in one cell; none has 'Min'/'Max'/'lower/upper' header or legend). Roles inferred by the producer from arithmetic (D=mean(C+2E), F=B+C+2E) -> dropped per instruction. Style A/B mapping of BA/BB and 'F belongs to Style A' also arithmetic-inferred.

Only d_nom, tpi, D (header 'Nominal Eye O.D.'), GA, GB ('Min Full Thread' Style A/B) survive: too thin to draw an eyebolt (no shank dia, eye ID, section dia, length). Publisher may prefer to reject the family.

torqbolt and fastenerz are numerically identical in the whole plain table and share the odd 1-1/8 BB=2.13 (4 other pages: 2.23) -> treat as one cluster to be safe; still AMES + TORQ/FZ + NL = 3 clusters on kept columns.
nan-long is a Boltport-family copy (shared '9/15' typo) - counted as one cluster; its 9/16 row cannot be matched by label (size printed '9/15').

rows 1-1/8 and 2 were dropped by the producer only because of BB; with BB columns dropped, D/GA/GB/tpi for these rows are agreed by all 4 pages (D 4.06/6.88, GA 2.31/3.38, GB 1.69/3.00, tpi 7/4.5) and could be restored (tpi for 2 is 4.5, non-integer).
shoulder-pattern extras in notes also rely on the same unlabeled min/max pairs and on Boltport-family pages -> do not publish them.
